title: AnyonWiki.org
authors: Colleen Delaney, Ralph Razzouk, Joost Slingerland, Gert Vercleyen
abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.
summary: This paper introduces the AnyonWiki, an open-source project providing a comprehensive database of fusion rings and fusion categories. It serves as a crucial resource for classifying topological matter models, such as those exhibiting anyonic excitations. By standardizing and digitizing this complex data, the project significantly aids theoretical research in topological quantum field theories and condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The project aims to create an accessible, verifiable, and usable resource for the complex algebraic and numerical data associated with fusion and unitary modular fusion categories.
main_result: The AnyonWikiDatabase currently catalogs over 25,000 fusion rings and includes classifications of multiplicity-free pivotal fusion categories up to rank 7.
method: The data is managed in an open-source database structure (JSON files) and presented via a dedicated website, adhering to FAIR data principles for reproducibility.
model_or_system: The underlying mathematical structures are fusion categories and fusion rings, which provide a framework for classifying anyons and defects in gapped topological phases of matter and TQFTs.
key_observables: Fusion coefficients, F-symbols, R-symbols, S-matrix, and Frobenius–Perron dimensions.
important_parameters: Rank of the fusion category (up to 10 for rings), and the specific algebraic properties (e.g., pivotal, braided, unitary) of the category.
main_assumptions: The data structure is designed to be expandable, and contributions require linking data to a DOI or detailed software dictionary.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the count of fusion categories up to rank 7 possessing various structural properties (pivotal, braided, etc.), while Table 1 shows the count of available fusion rings by rank and multiplicity.
paper_structure: The article discusses the scientific motivation for the database, details the contents and structure of the AnyonWikiDatabase, and outlines contribution guidelines for maintaining data integrity.
why_interesting: The classification of anyons and topological phases is central to understanding exotic quantum matter, making the underlying mathematical framework highly relevant to condensed matter theory.

By definition, the ribbon fusion categories belong to the intersection of the braided and spherical squares. Each number indi- cates the number of fusion categories that lie in the connected region of the Venn diagram. There are thus, e.g., 0 fusion categories with no compatible extra struc- tures (since all the categories found admit a pivotal structure), 31 pivotal fusion categories with no compatible extra structures, 185 ribbon fusion categories that are neither modular nor unitary, 109 fusion categories that are modular and uni- tary, 229 fusion categories...
